narrative: The model estimated your probability of being a bad credit risk at 45%, meaning that among applicants with a similar profile, about 45 in 100 would be expected to represent higher credit risk. Under the bank’s decision rule, that risk level was high enough to deny the application; it does not mean default is certain. Of the factors that most affected the decision, the size of the loan you requested ranked first, the state of your checking account second, and the share of disposable income your installments would use third. The requested amount actually worked in your favor: 2,712 was below the approved-applicant average of 3,019.64. Your checking-account status was the main unfavorable influence among these top factors: a negative balance below 0 DM is uncommon among approved applicants, at 12.6%, and it pushed the assessment toward bad credit. Your installment burden also worked in your favor: 2.00% of disposable income was below the approved average of 2.99, suggesting a lighter repayment load. The denial therefore came from the combined effect of all factors, with the checking-account signal being the clearest concern among the top three. Next, bring your checking account into good standing, avoid overdrafts, reduce existing credit obligations, and gather current income and employment evidence. Ask the bank whether it will reconsider after these changes or with a guarantor, and request specific feedback on what would most improve a future application.
